## Verdict
- Answer: Probably yes in tone, but I could not measure it. No Prism calls were run. From memory, the literature moved from "ESG does not hurt returns" (2015) to sustained skepticism about performance, ratings, and real-world impact (2020 onward) (est.).
- Decision: Treat ESG-performance claims as contested. Do not rely on a single "ESG pays" study. Demand evidence on impact, ratings quality, and greenwashing before committing capital or policy.
- Confidence: low - this rests on recalled landmark papers, not a systematic yearly orientation count.
- What would change it: A classified yearly count of ESG papers (positive vs critical) that shows a flat or falling critical share.

## What the data shows
No counted series exists in this run. Only recalled facts are given, each tagged.

- A meta-analysis of over 2,000 empirical studies found about 90% reported a non-negative ESG–financial performance relation [r1].
- Rating disagreement is large: correlations between major ESG raters averaged about 0.54 [r2], versus about 0.99 for credit ratings (est.).
- A study of US funds found that PRI signatories did not improve portfolio companies' ESG compliance [r3].
- A study of SEC-registered ESG funds found they often held companies with worse compliance records than non-ESG peers [r4].

The chart is an illustrative estimate of the critical share, not a measurement. Values are my guesses for the direction of travel and should not be cited as data.

That is a different quantity from the baseline, so no single ratio is valid. The claim is that the framing shifted from "does it pay" to "does it measure or achieve anything".

- [r2] Berg, Kölbel, Rigobon, 2022, Review of Finance, peer-reviewed. Supports the critical measurement framing. Quote not reproduced, since I cannot verify exact wording.

- [r4] Adams, Mehran, and colleagues (Fed/industry working paper lineage), year uncertain. Treat as weak, unverified.

## Verdict
- Answer: No. In this corpus, ESG-investing research is not becoming more critical. The contested share fell from 24.8% in the early period to 15.7% in the late period [c1], while "promising" framing grew fastest. The 2025 contested share (24.9% [c1]) is back near early levels, so the trend is not clean.
- Decision: Treat "the literature is turning against ESG" as unsupported. Do not treat "the literature has settled" as supported either. Watch whether 2025 is a rebound.
- Confidence: low-medium - orientation labels describe how a paper frames its own finding, not whether it is right [c1]. The corpus starts in 2017 and the phrase set is broad.
- What would change it: 2026 data showing a contested share staying above ~25%, or a check on a narrower "ESG" phrase set.

## What the data shows
The corpus holds 782 papers for 2017–2025 under the phrases "esg investing", "sustainable investment", "responsible investing" and "socially responsible investing" [c1]. Yearly volume rose from 63 in 2017 to 342 in 2025 [c1].

Contested share (the sum of the critical-type orientations, as Prism defines it) by year [c1]: 19.0% in 2017, 27.1% in 2018, 27.1% in 2019, 26.6% in 2020, 8.3% in 2021, 27.0% in 2022, 12.1% in 2023, 6.8% in 2024, 24.9% in 2025.

Positive share [c1]: 12.7% in 2017, 5.1% in 2018, 22.9% in 2019, 19.6% in 2020, 6.2% in 2021, 5.3% in 2022, 25.4% in 2023, 30.6% in 2024, 26.3% in 2025.

Orientation totals over all years [c1]: promising 246, problem_identifying 180, descriptive 141, comparative 73, breakthrough 52, cautionary 49, critical 41.

The strict "critical" label is rare. It had 5 papers in 2017 and 9 in 2025 [c1], a late-vs-early ratio of 2.0 [c1], which is less than the growth in total volume. Problem-identifying papers rose from 4 to 69 [c1], with a late-vs-early ratio of 2.49 [c1].

## Trend
```prism-chart
{"id":"contested_share","kind":"line","title":"Share of papers framed as contested, by year","unit":"% of papers","window":{"from":"2017-01-01","to":"2025-12-31"},"x":{"field":"year","type":"temporal"},"series":[{"name":"contested_pct","source":"call:research.stance_trends#1","points":[["2017",19.0],["2018",27.1],["2019",27.1],["2020",26.6],["2021",8.3],["2022",27.0],["2023",12.1],["2024",6.8],["2025",24.9]]},{"name":"positive_pct","source":"call:research.stance_trends#1","points":[["2017",12.7],["2018",5.1],["2019",22.9],["2020",19.6],["2021",6.2],["2022",5.3],["2023",25.4],["2024",30.6],["2025",26.3]]}],"caption":"Contested share is volatile and ends 2025 near its early level after a 2024 low.","supports":"The 2025 contested share (24.9% [c1]) is back near early levels, so the trend is not clean."}
```
Early-vs-late contested share: 24.8% to 15.7%, a change of -9.1 percentage points [c1]. Prism's own reading is "recent work is markedly more positive than earlier work" [c1]. The series is not monotonic. It dropped to 6.8% in 2024 and then rose by 18.1 points (24.9 − 6.8, computed from [c1]) in 2025. The 2025 jump is driven by 69 problem-identifying papers [c1].

## Comparison
Baseline: the early-period contested share of 24.8% [c1], compared with the late-period share of 15.7% [c1] on the same scale (% of papers).
- Delta: -9.1 points [c1]. Ratio: about 0.63 (15.7 / 24.8, computed from [c1]).
- Promising: late-vs-early count ratio 7.31 [c1], against 2.0 for critical [c1]. Counts are the sum of the early third versus the late third (26 to 190 for promising, 8 to 16 for critical [c1]).
- In the sub-corpus filtered to "promising" papers, the stance summary is 27.9% positive and 37.3% contested [c2]. This is a different filter, so it is not comparable to the yearly series.

## Evidence
All items come from the Prism research index; none were read in full, so tier is not assessed (tier: unknown).
- [r1] Prism stance trends, 2017–2025 (c1): supports the verdict and the framing shift. No verbatim quote. Its caveat reads: "orientation is how a paper frames its own finding, not a verdict".
- [r2] Prism browse, filter "promising" (c2): W7163098966, 2025, "Behavioral interventions in ESG investing: … neobroker-based experiment" (promising, empirical). W7162301380, 2025, "Determinants of Sustainable Investment Intention" (promising). W7163603292, 2025, "Measuring the Impact of Socially Responsible Investments on Portfolio Performance Using the Shapley Value" (promising, methodological). W7124577558, 2025, "Monitoring Potential of Sustainable Investment of a Cemetery Land…" (promising), which is off-topic for ESG finance and shows noise from the broad phrase.
- Critical examples: I did not retrieve critical or cautionary papers, so I cannot give critical paper IDs. See follow-up f1.

## Drill-down
Layers available: year (9 years), orientation (7 labels), contribution type (empirical 885, review 205, position 177, methodological 144, theoretical 43 [c2]), and topic (Sustainable Finance and Green Bonds 538, Corporate Social Responsibility Reporting 418 [c2]). Note that these facet counts cover the whole subject and exceed the 782 in [c1], so the two use different scopes.

## Method and limits
- Window: 2017–2025. The end is 2025-12-31 at latest, about 10 months before today (2026-10-23). 2026 is not covered.

Phrase audit by title: sustainable investment 714, esg investing 225, responsible investing 225, socially responsible investing 148 [c2]. The set is dominated by "sustainable investment", which pulls in off-topic papers such as the cemetery land study. This expansion can dilute any ESG-specific critical trend.
